traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Coriariaceae: leaves usually opposite, rarely whorled; leaves simple; margins entire or dentate; veins palmate or parallel; blades lanceolate, oblanceolate, oblong or ovate; stipules present; plants hermaphrodite, monoecious or polygamous; ovary superior; floral cup absent; stems woody; flowers in racemes; flowers actinomorphic; perianth sepals and petals; fruit achene; parts of each whorl 5; stamens 10; carpels 5 (-10). Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.
